answer: Persistent divergence tracking. Each identity must publish a per-epoch behavioural vector; the system computes drift between consecutive vectors and flags any identity whose drift exceeds a learned reef of normal variance. A genuine agent produces only a small ripple across epochs, while a sybil cluster spawning fresh identities shows discontinuous jumps detectable against the wider ocean of established histories. Detection forces attackers to slowly mature every fake identity over many epochs, multiplying time and compute cost per identity.
